H2OH01194.name: Greg Landsman
H2OH01194.bio: Former public school teacher and Cincinnati City Council member who now represents Southwest Ohio in Congress.

positions.stance: Believes "we need to hold price-gougers accountable and stop corporations from jacking up prices at the expense of middle class families."
Focused on investing in job training and small businesses, raising the minimum wage, and protecting the right to organize.
Working to codify Roe v. Wade, ensure access to birth control, and protect IVF treatment.
Will fight for increased public school funding and better teacher pay, lower college costs, and more career and technical education.
Focused on returning taxpayer dollars to Southwest Ohio "to fix our roads, bridges, and waterlines."

H6OH01138.name: Eric Conroy
H6OH01138.bio: Former U.S. Air Force intelligence officer and CIA case officer.

positions.stance: "Will fight to lower inflation, cut red tape, and champion pro-growth policies that put Ohio workers and small businesses first."
"Will stand with law enforcement, oppose defunding the police, and fight for policies that keep violent criminals off our streets."
Will secure the southern border "with stronger enforcement, smarter technology, and policies that stop illegal immigration."
Will fight for infrastructure investments that "reduce congestion, improve roads and bridges, and ensure taxpayer dollars are spent wisely."
"Will empower parents, support local control, and expand career-focused education to prepare students for real-world success."

H4OH02248.name: David Taylor
H4OH02248.bio: Former local prosecutor and owner of his family business in Clermont County, Ohio.

positions.stance: Describes himself as "a pro-life conservative" who believes "the unborn deserve to be protected by the law," prioritizing adoption and child care access.
Will author legislation requiring Congress "to balance the budget before they get paid," and supports cutting taxes and expanding fossil fuel and nuclear energy.
Will fight to secure the border "by finishing President Trump's wall, increasing funding and resources for Border Patrol officers, and deploying military personnel when necessary."
Calls the Second Amendment "clear and unequivocal" and says "I will always vote to protect it."
Supports "defunding and dismantling" the Department of Education, "restoring parental rights, and expanding school choice."

H6OH04082.name: Jim Jordan
H6OH04082.bio: Congressman for Ohio's 4th District and chairman of the House Judiciary Committee; former Ohio state legislator.

H6OH04181.name: Joshua Kolasinski
H6OH04181.bio: Small business owner who installs, tests, and repairs medical equipment.

positions.stance: Proposes a "First ever Registered Voter Lobby" and a district think tank with input from residents, favoring "data driven, smart solutions."
Says "Full-time work deserves economic stability" and would "Prioritize workers over shareholders."
Would allow Medicare to negotiate drug prices, increase price transparency, and explore public and private options that reduce costs.
Would integrate mental and emotional wellness into health care and "Treat addiction as health issue instead of moral failure."
Would prioritize infrastructure spending using local labor, expand rural high-speed internet, and upgrade water and power systems.

H6OH05154.name: Brian Shaver
H6OH05154.bio: President of the Fostoria City Council and social studies teacher at Fostoria Junior/Senior High School.

positions.stance: Supports helping farmers, investing in affordable rural housing, and lowering medication costs; says "the wealthiest Americans should pay the same tax rate as everyone else."
Says sweeping tariffs hurt farmers, Congress should check the president's actions, and large-scale foreign farmland purchases must be addressed.
Says his "first responsibility as an elected official is to uphold the U.S. Constitution" and executive actions resembling lawmaking should be challenged.
Believes the federal government "must fund schools adequately" and opposes micromanaging classrooms with "excessive testing, censorship, or rigid mandates."
"I won't support laws that elevate one religion over another or push the United States toward becoming a theocracy."

H4OH06165.name: Michael Rulli
H4OH06165.bio: Congressman for Ohio's 6th District, former Ohio state senator and Leetonia School Board president, and co-owner of Rulli Brothers Market.

positions.stance: Calls to "Abolish Ice," saying "Due Process is a right; not a privilege" and any entity that prohibits basic constitutional rights "should not exist."
Supports fair and safe voting in all elections, where "every American gets have one vote; no more and no less."
Supports legislation requiring news outlets "to adhere to ethical dissemination of truthful speech and information."
Supports codifying Roe, calling abortion "a choice that is between a woman, her doctor, and her God."
Pledges to protect First Amendment freedoms of religion, speech, press, assembly, and petition.

H2OH16051.name: Max Miller
H2OH16051.bio: Congressman for Ohio's 7th District; former White House Director of Presidential Advance and senior advisor to President Trump, and Marine Corps Reserve veteran.

positions.stance: Has voted to support "making tax cuts permanent, no tax on tips, and no tax on overtime."
Aims to "expand workforce development and career and technical education opportunities," saying the American dream does not require a four-year degree.
"Max will fight for increased funding and support for law enforcement."
"Max will continue to fight to maintain the secure border."
Supports Trump administration policies "to develop American energy independence and reduce the costs of gas and electricity."

H6OH07168.name: Brian Poindexter
H6OH07168.bio: Union ironworker and Brook Park city councilman.

positions.stance: Says he has "a plan to bring down the prices of gas, groceries, and health care."
"Working families are paying more while corporations post record profits. An economy that works should work for the people who power it."
"Every worker deserves the freedom to organize without intimidation."
"I will fight to bring down the cost of insurance and prescription drugs while protecting rural hospitals."
"We shouldn't reward companies for shipping jobs overseas."

H6OH08315.name: Warren Davidson
H6OH08315.bio: Congressman for Ohio's 8th District; West Point graduate and former Army Ranger who spent 15 years starting and growing Ohio manufacturing companies.

positions.stance: "I oppose the income tax," favoring a tax on consumption "with exclusions for food, clothing, shelter, healthcare, etc."
Says the Second Amendment must protect individual gun rights; opposes "red flag laws, expanded restrictions on lawful transfers, magazine bans, and others."
Supports a House Healthcare Committee, ending health insurers' antitrust exemption, HSAs for all, and block-granting federal Medicaid per citizen.
Supports police and promoting "honest judges who apply the law rather than act as lawmakers."
Supports President Trump's National Security Strategy, "peace through strength," and "a predisposition to non-interventionism with a high bar for the use of force."

H8OH08097.name: Vanessa Enoch
H8OH08097.bio: Leads Cultural Impact, LLC, a management and technology consulting firm, and works as a public policy consultant and community organizer.

positions.stance: Supports "responsible gun laws that protect both constitutional rights and public safety," including safe storage, background checks, and Ethan's Law.
Says new technologies like AI "should be developed carefully and ethically," with data centers responsibly managing power, water, and energy resources.
Supports "rewriting land-use rules, investing in mixed-income developments," and ensuring teachers, nurses and firefighters can live near their workplaces.
Would empower Medicare and Medicaid to negotiate drug prices, cap out-of-pocket costs, fund community clinics, and invest in preventive care.
Supports negotiating prescription-drug prices, expanding preventive care, "raising the minimum wage and investing in education and child care."

H2OH09031.name: Marcy Kaptur
H2OH09031.bio: Member of Congress from Northwest Ohio running for reelection.

positions.stance: Fighting to lower utility bills, expand affordable housing, fully fund Medicare and Medicaid, restore ACA tax credits, and lower child and elder care costs.
Supports ending "tax breaks for companies that ship jobs overseas" and expanding workforce training; opposed NAFTA and pushed to crack down on China's trade practices.
Supports working together "to enforce our immigration laws, deport violent criminals, and give law enforcement the resources they need" while protecting due process.
Fighting "to grow more of our food here at home" and support small and family-owned farms.
Will keep working "to protect our drinking water, combat harmful algal blooms and invasive species" in Lake Erie.

H4OH09169.name: Derek Merrin
H4OH09169.bio: Former Ohio state representative and Ohio House Republican Caucus leader, former mayor of Waterville, and real estate investor.

H2OH03067.name: Mike Turner
H2OH03067.bio: Congressman and senior member of the House Armed Services Committee; former two-term Mayor of Dayton and corporate lawyer.

positions.stance: Highlights growing and retaining manufacturing, defense industry and high tech jobs, including attracting Fuyao to the former GM plant.
Pushing for legislative fixes "to increase access to substance abuse treatment for those most vulnerable in the opioid epidemic, including babies born addicted."
Highlights doubling jobs at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base and bringing federal funding and new jobs there during the BRAC process.
Works "to prevent irresponsible and devastating cuts to our military" and to ensure service members have the tools and support they need.
Says he worked across the aisle to pass annual reforms aimed at eradicating sexual assault from the military.

H6OH10121.name: Kristina Knickerbocker
H6OH10121.bio: U.S. Air Force veteran and oncology nurse practitioner.

positions.stance: Will "ban stock trading for members of Congress, end corporate PAC influence, pass term limits, protect voting rights," and curb the lobbying revolving door.
Will cut taxes for working families, repeal tariffs, build affordable housing, cap childcare costs, and make corporations pay for data center infrastructure.
Believes "healthcare is a right"; will work toward universal coverage, protect Medicaid, Medicare and the ACA, and support a public option.
"I'll invest in law enforcement, fire departments, and prevention strategies that strengthen safety while building trust in our communities."
Will "fully fund and protect the VA, defend and grow Wright-Patterson Air Force Base," and support military families.

H2OH11169.name: Shontel Brown
H2OH11169.bio: U.S. Representative for Ohio's 11th District since 2021; former Cuyahoga County Councilmember and Warrensville Heights City Councilmember.

H6OH11210.name: Mike Krichner
H6OH11210.bio: Retired consultant with 30 years of experience evaluating mostly pension plans.

H8OH12180.name: Troy Balderson
H8OH12180.bio: Congressman who grew up working on his family's farm in Zanesville.

positions.stance: Supports closing "the open borders," going after cartels, hiring "more border patrol officers and fewer IRS agents," and ending sanctuary cities.
Would streamline permits, build pipelines, "Repeal the radical green agenda," and "Allow consumers to choose the vehicle that is best for their own needs."
Supports lifting "the Biden LNG export ban to expand energy markets and support our European allies."
Working "to lower inflation, reduce taxes, and put money back in your wallet"; says "Stop spending what we don't have."
Supports forcing the sale of TikTok to an American company, bringing manufacturing back, and reversing "the Biden EV mandate."

H4OH12080.name: Jerrad Christian
H4OH12080.bio: Software engineer and U.S. Navy veteran who served as a flight deck fueler and meteorologist.

positions.stance: Would "end Citizens United, cap campaign spending," and bar foreign-linked organizations, including AIPAC, from influencing officials through campaign cash.
Supports passing the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act to restore protections removed after Shelby County v. Holder.
Says Congress "must pass and codify expanded protections for civil rights, reproductive rights, marriage equality, and religious freedom."
Supports abolishing ICE as it exists, replacing it with "a narrowly tailored, accountable system," and prosecuting agents who break the law.
Supports passing universal healthcare, saying it is "proven to lower costs while removing the middle men."

H2OH13264.name: Emilia Sykes
H2OH13264.bio: U.S. Representative for Ohio's 13th Congressional District.

positions.stance: Says "access to clean water, clean air, and a clean environment is a basic human right" and supports environmentally friendly policies that support the economy.
Supports the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Act and the Freedom to Vote Act to make it easier to vote.
Co-sponsored the EDUCATORS for America Act and American Teacher Act; wants affordable post-high-school options without crushing student loan debt.
Running "to keep jobs from going overseas" and supports investing in American manufacturing, job training, and apprenticeships.
Pushing to cap the cost of medications such as insulin and expand affordable long-term care; opposes cuts to Medicaid.

H6OH13307.name: Carey Coleman
H6OH13307.bio: Northeast Ohio radio host on WNIR and longtime TV meteorologist.

positions.stance: Supports "reining in out-of-control federal spending," ending wasteful programs, and unleashing American energy production to lower fuel and utility costs.
Will advocate for more resources for local police, "stronger penalties for violent and repeat offenders," and cracking down on fentanyl trafficking.
Will "defend the First and Second Amendments, protect religious freedom, and work to rein in unelected agencies."
Supports pro-growth tax policies, regulatory reform for small businesses, workforce training, and reshoring critical manufacturing and supply chains.
Supports "streamlining federal permitting" and prioritizing repair and modernization of existing infrastructure, with transparent oversight and performance-based funding.

H2OH14064.name: David Joyce
H2OH14064.bio: Representative for Ohio's 14th Congressional District and former Geauga County Prosecutor.

H6OH14248.name: Maria Jukic
H6OH14248.bio: Attorney with a healthcare career and former city councilwoman.

positions.stance: Believes healthcare "is a basic human right"; would lower the Medicare eligibility age to 62 and let Medicare negotiate drug prices.
Will fight for ratepayer protections so utilities don't spread data-center grid costs to residents, and opposes fast-tracking approvals or preempting local zoning.
Would "Expand the Child Tax Credit and boost federal childcare funding so no Ohio family pays more for daycare than they would for in-state tuition."
Will push for trade policies that open markets for Ohio farm products and support lower input costs and affordable crop insurance.
Will push for a federal framework guaranteeing protections such as knowing when you're interacting with AI and human review for major decisions.

H6OH15112.name: Don Leonard
H6OH15112.bio: Professor of city and regional planning at Ohio State and former U.S. Peace Corps volunteer.

positions.stance: "One job should be enough to buy a home, raise a family, and retire with dignity."
Supports "universal healthcare, affordable childcare, paid family leave, and support for those who care for an aging parent or a disabled loved one."
"Democracy should mean one person, one vote. Not one dollar, one vote."
Says everyone deserves to live "free from fear of discrimination, violence, or government harassment" and to have equality under the justice system.
Says development "should protect our water, strengthen the electric grid, create good local jobs, and earn the community's trust."

H6GA01158.name: Amanda Hollowell
H6GA01158.bio: Political strategist and Chief of Campaigns at Color Of Change; previously directed national organizing at When We All Vote.

positions.stance: Will "fully fund rural hospitals, expand mental health services, and protect Medicaid from harmful cuts."
Supports "expanding apprenticeship programs, protecting the right to organize," and making sure federal investments reach workers.
Will champion federal investment in flood protection, resilient infrastructure, and clean energy jobs, and fight to preserve the Okefenokee.
Supports "restoring voting rights, expanding access to the ballot box, and standing up to gerrymandering and voter suppression."
Supports "national paid family and medical leave" so families can care for loved ones without losing their jobs.
